Splitting Deathly Hallows into two movies was, undeniably, a corporate plot to double box office profits. But giving the story some time to breathe for the first time in seven movies did pay some dividends. Deathly Hallows part one is admittedly light on plot but, considering the dearth of proper character development in the last six movies, it was a welcome change of pace.

The riskiest jump from any Potter movie: moving away from Hogwarts. The fugitive feel is a nice change of pace for the first half of this final entry, with the final pieces of the story laying themselves nicely for an action-packed finale.

I remember this being the “boring one” (and likewise the portion of the book it covers). That assessment was perhaps a little misguided. On rewatch I actually enjoyed the slower pace. The studio’s decision to split the last book into two movies may have been a financial one, but it works out for the best, artistically speaking. Characters are allowed their moments, and the actors are, for the most part, up to the task. It feels deserved, and almost necessary, for pt 1 to take its time in this way. I was never bored—the opposite actually. I stayed up way too late watching it all on TV. Bumping my rating up a star for the nick cave song, which I totally forgot was in this.

Qué lugar tan hermoso... para estar con amigos Desde que inició sabía que pegaría fuerte y lo hizo, el inicio y final de esta cinta puede hacerte llorar. De nuevo se cumple otras muertes en esta película. Verla con otros ojos no recordaba ciertas cosas como el odio de los magos oscuros contra los muggles y esa parte cuando toman control del ministerio de magia me parece aterradora donde comienza una caza a los mestizos interesante analogía del racismo llevada al mundo mágico. La parte del cuento de los 3 hermanos esta hermosa tanto visual como en la narrativa ese cambio a una animación le quedó perfecto a esa escena sin problemas puede pasar como un cortometraje fuera del mundo de HP. La dialogación esta muy bien, tiene muy drama y peso para los personajes en especial ese baile de Hermione y Harry con O Children de fondo; lo que no me gustó son algunas escenas que la pantalla verde se nota mucho y hace que uno se concentré más en eso. Fun fact: Cuando salió por 1ra vez no entendía porque habia terminado tan repentinamente la película, no sabía que habría una segunda parte aunque en el título lo dijera.

People who say they don't like this one because its boring or there isn't any action is CRAZY. This one is literal nonstop action for 2.5hrs?? I've never understood that critique. And I LOVE LOVE LOVE the Tale of Three Brother’s animation (another thing people complain about). Also Scabior is so hot in this!!! What's not to love?? "THESE ARE DARK TIMES THERE IS NO DENYING." I love Bill Nighy's voice lol Another great opening. It is TRAGIC showing Hermione obliviate her parents, and that song is one of the best in the whole series too. Following that with Snape's entrance: Alan Rickman in these final movies is just INCREDIBLE. His fabulous entrance, and his FACE. It breaks me. I love the seven Harrys scene. The polyjuice moment is hilarious, the Hedwig death is shocking and devastating, and then the moment with Voldemort (literally “flying death”) is brilliant! I love his anger bursting out of him when Malfoy's wand doesn't work like expected. The naked snogging vision from the horcrux is wildddd. Still jarring to this day. Not giving us the Peter Pettigrew death was criminal. The whole mirror situation must be so confusing to anyone who didnt read the books. That little shard of glass that is never explained with a random old man staring back and then sending Dobby? This needed to be done wayyy better or should've been scrapped entirely. The Bellatrix knife throw in slow-mo is orgasmic to me. Sad the knife ended up in Dobby, of course. That final scene with Voldemort though!! What a FANTASTIC way to end part 1. (Obviously a money grab, but they did it all so damn well.)
